key_insight: Exponential shear testing can recover both the steady shear flow curve and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve by accounting for evolving deformation and stress directions.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables broader characterization of complex-fluid rheology using commercial strain-controlled rheometers that measure time-varying torque and normal force.
method: Impose an exponentially increasing shear deformation.
Analyze the evolving eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the flow kinematics and sample stress.
Define material functions that map measurements to shear and planar extensional viscosity curves.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports support from nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive-model simulations, asymptotic analysis, and experiments with several polymeric liquids.
watch_item: Reliable implementation requires accurate transient torque and normal-force measurements; applicability beyond the tested polymeric liquids remains to be established.
paper_title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
